## Chapt. III.

### *VVhere it is shevved that Antichrist is come alreadye.*

Concerning the comming of Antichrist, we haue set downe demonstrations at the beginning of this Confutation, which maye moderate and determine each of questions in this cause, so as they may make manifest the truth of each of them. Yet least this place, where the point is handled of purpose, should complaine, that it is left naked and empty; it shall not be amisse; to adde one or two reasons more to the former, as an ouerplus. And these we take out of the **2. Thess. 2. 2.** and first out of the third verse; Where it is said, *vnlesse the Apostasy come first, and that man of sinne be reuealed, that Sonne of perdition, &c.* In which words the Apostle affirmeth, both that each of these two things shall goe before the comming of Christ, as also, that the Apostasy shall goe before the reuealing of Antichrist. For that is the cause of this, that procureth this mischeife, as he teacheth after, that Antichrist shall therfore come, because men vvould not receaue the loue of the truth that they might be saued; **vers. 10. 11.** And the reuealing of Antichrist should not be delayed after the Apostasy, but it commeth forthwith after it; as the Apostle saith, *vnlesse the apostasy come first, and the man of sinne be reuealed, &c.* For after that that which hindereth should be taken awaye, which as we haue shewed, came to passe shortly after, this pestilent Antichrist should come abroad into the world immediatly.

But this apostasy began priuily and closely at first, euen in the time of the Apostle, which therfore can not be a reuolt from the Romane Empire, but a neglect and contempt of the truth that was once receaued, as the same Apostle doth interprete it in that place, and it is that which hath preuailed for these many ages last past, and is to be seene openly at this day in that worshipping of reliques and of Images, and in the inuocation of Saints practised by the Church of Rome, as we haue

### Chapt. IV.

#### *Against the first demonstration that Antichrist is not yet come, taken from the Vniuersall preaching of the Gospel.*

Tis question about the time of Antichrist comming, geueth greatest light to the truth of all the rest, being as it were the sunne that enlighteneth al the rest of the starres with his light; Hereuppon it is that Bellarmine hath præpared sixe thight and thicke vailes, which he calleth demonstrations, to obscure the truth with, vnder which he hopes his Pope may lurke safely. Nowe he will haue these taken out of so many certaine signes (as he saith) of antichrists comming, two whereof doe goe before, namely the preaching of the Gospell in the whole world, and the desolation of the Romane Empire.

For antichrist was to come for rejecting the loue of the Truth, 2. Thess. 2. 10. Nowe the punishment is not inflicted before the fault be committed ; and there could be no such fault made, before there were power & meanes geuen to knowe and to beleeue the truth.

Theſe things and many of the like nature doe make it plaine, that howeſoeuer the doctrine of ſaluation haue ſhined vpon many nations before Antichriſt came, yet after he ſhalbe once defaced, the Tabernacles of the Holy truth ſhalbe vnfolded much wider; ſo that a very huge and innumerable multitude ſhal be gathered together into them; vnto which the aſſemblies of former times being compared ſhall ſeeme to be very ſmall, or rather none at all. Theſe things are thoſe which the Scriptures teach touching the vniuerſall preaching, which be conſtant, firme, ſtable, full of Maieſty, power, and mercy in reſpect of God, but if we ſhall caſt our eyes vppon our ſelues, they are no leſſe full fraught with al kinde of ioye, and Solace. Whereas on the contrary thoſe things which you haue ſet before vs, are either vncertaine coniectures, or vaine fictions and forgeries, which will both deceaue your expectation at the laſt, and in the meane time, they leade you away into errour and deſtruction.

## Chapt. V.

### *Against Bellarmines ſecond demonſtration taken from the deſolation of the Romane Empire.*

The ſecond demonſtration is taken (as you ſay) from another ſigne that goeth before the time of *Antichrist*,vvhich ſhalbe a totall deſolation of the *Romane Empire*,vvhich ſeing it endureth to this daye, *Antichrist* is not yet come. Herevppon you vndertake to proue tvvo things;both that *Antichriſt* vvill not come til after that the Empire of *Rome* be altogether laid vvaſt; and then that the Empire of *Rome* endureth vnto this daye. You confirme the firſt out of foure ſcriptures. Among vvhich the three firſt,namely *Dan.2.*and *7.Reuel,17.* Relye vppon the interpretation of *Ireneus,Book 5.*

But I pray you let vs let authorities of men goe, and let vs vvaigh the matter it ſelfe in the ballance of the truth. If the matter vvere to be ſifted out vvith the opinions of men,that are contrary each to others, and vvhereof many might be brought in theſe moſt darke and obſcure places, vve ſhould neuer make an ende. Let vs vvorke it rather out of thoſe principles,by the cõduct vvhereof vve may be lead to ſomewhat that is certaine.

As touching therfore the ſecond of *Daniel*,and that ſucceſſion of the cheife Kingdomes, vvhich vvere to be on earth to the end of the vvorld,vvhich the *Image* ſheweth, that noteth out by the head of *Gold*, the breaſt of *Siluer*, the Belly of *braſſe*, the legges of *iron* and the feete partly of *iron*, partly of *claye*, the foure principall Kingdomes that ſhould be on earth, namely; Of the *Aſſyrians*, the *Perſians*,the *Grecians*,the *Romanes*, vvhereof that of the *Romanes*,vvhich is the laſt,*vvas* as you ſay,diuided into tvvo parts for a moſt longe time, as the legges are tvvo and longeſt of all the parts. Beſides that there ſprung vp ten toes out of thoſe tvvo legges,and that the vvhole *Image* ended in them, becauſe the *Romane Empire* vvas to be diuided at length into ten *Kings*,becauſe there ſhalbe no *King* of the *Romanes*,as no toe is a legge. As touching theſe things I ſaye, vvhat one vvord is there in this vvhole viſion, vvhereby *Antichriſt* comming may be intimated,

mated, after the vtter defacing of the Empire of Rome? I heare of two legges, & feete diuided into ten Toes, but not the least hint touching Antichrist, whether he should come or no, or whether he should come after this diuision or before it, or in the time of it. Doe you thus goe on to build demonstrations, or rather castles in the aire, without any least shewe of a ground for them to stand on? Nay what if the contrary may be most firmely concluded from hence, that Antichrist should come before the vniuersall destruction of this Impire? But these feete are the Empire of Rome, which is weaker, then that was of the Legges, which yet was the Romane Empire also. For the statue described onely foure Kingdomes; but if the Legges and the Feete betokened a diuerse Kingdome, there should be fiue. Neither is that of any value, which you say, that A toe is not a Legge, seeing no one member is another, though both of them be parts of the same entire thing, euen as the Legge and the toe are parts of the fourth Kingdome. Nowe then you see howe sweetly you haue demonstrated the nakednes of your cause, which the more you labour to couer and hide, the more foule and manifest doe you make it.

Wherefore the ten Hornes doe by no meanes signifie the destruction and fall of the Romane Empire, so that they can yeeld vs no helpe to finde out the comming of Antichrist. <header>TOUCHING ANTICHRIST. chap. 5.</header>

And indeed Gregory said not well, *All things are done vvhich vvere foretold, the King of Pride is neere*, if any such desolation were to be expected, as you speake of, or if such ten Kings should come forth before, as you Papists tell vs Tales of. Therefore either those Fathers knewe not what that was which hindred, or els they floated hether & thether with their doubtfull opinions, so as no sound and stable thing can be gathered out of their writings. But theis Booke of the Reuelation; being nowe made cleare by the Euent & that for the most part, makes the matter to be without all question, as also it doth expound Paul most certainly and most faithfully, teaching vs that that which hindereth, is not the Romane Empire, but the sixth Romane King; for he saith; *fiue are fallen, one, namely, the sixth, is novve, the other is not yet come*, Reuel. 1. 10.

That is, the heathen Emperours, who make the sixth Kinge, and doe nowe raigne, who being at length taken awaye, and leauing Rome emptye for the Pope of Rome, the seauenth King shal come, that is, that Antichrist.

The Romane Empire is one after a sort, but the manner of gouerning it by diuerse Magistrats, and kinds of gouerning, is manifold. And it could not be said, fiue Romane Empires haue fallen, but fiue Kings, who were Rulars & Gouernours of that one Empire. Besides, Antichrist is that seauenth Romane King; for so saith the Angell expressely; *And the Beast, vvhich vvas, and is not, is both that eighth King, and one of the seauen*, vers. 11.

What should the Romane Empire be made desolate, while it had a King thereof remaining aliue and alive-like? no such matter, but rather the whore of Rome should flourish exceedingly, where she should be carried on the backe of this Kinglike Beast. Therfore the Romane Empire was not to be destroyed, when Antichrist was to come, but it is rather to be meruailously preserued, increased, and amplified, during the time foreappointed by God. Let vs therfore vnderstand that Paul & Iohn speake of the same impediment, but the Angel doth describe it more expressely and clearely, by the place, the dignity of it and the nomber, by which as by most plaine and true signes we should be lead as it were by the hand to the very cradle and infancy of Antichrist.

For this feruitude of theirs hath proceeded so farre, that they haue taken his marke and then haue taken and kept the Oathe of Fealty to him, not to speake of the rest of those most villanous wayes, by which the Beast hath troden the Soueraigne Maiesty of the Emperours vnder his feete.

Lastly the Toes of his feete being nowe diuided, are not nowe kept in with any common bande of the Imperiall name, but onely of the whore of Rome.

### Chapt. VI.

#### Against the third demonstration taken from the comming of *Henoch*, and *Elias*.

SO much for the signe, that should by your reckoning goe before your Antichrists comming; nowe we come to those that you say must accompany him, as it were his *Legats a latere*, and first of the comming of *Henoch* and *Elias*, who as you say, are still liuing, & liue for this ende, that they might oppose themselues against Antichrist vvhen he commeth, and might preserue the elect in the faith of *Christ*; and might cou- uert the *Ievves* at last, all vvhich though, it is most certaine that they be not fulfilled. In this cause you vse three arguments, the first drawne out of the Scriptures, the second out of the Fathers, the third from reason. The Scriptures you bring are foure; *Malach.* 4.5.6. *Ecclesiast.* 48.9.10. and againe, 44.16. *Math.* 17.11. *Reuel.* 11.3. As touching *Malachy* his words are; *Behold I vvill send vnto you Elias the Prophet, before that great day of the Lord shall come, and he shall conuert the hearts of the Fathers to the children, and the hearts of the children to their Fathers*, vvhich vvords can not (as you say) be vnderstood of any kinde of *Doctors*, as of *Luther*, *Zvvinglius*, and the like; For *malachy* saith, that the *Ievves* are to be conuerted by *Elias*, and that he should be sent for the *Ievves* sake principally, as it is eui- dent by that; *I wil send vnto you*, and that of *Ecclesiasticus*, *he shal restore the Tribes of Iacob*; but say you, *Luther* and *Zvvinglius* haue conuerted neuer a *Ievve* in their liues. But Malachy speakes of a double comming of the Lord, and besides he is to be understood figuratiuely of the first, for so Christ interpreteth them, saying that the Baptist is that Elias that is to come. Therefore he is to be understood to speake figuratiuely also touching the second; and such an Elias is nowe to be looked for of vs from this prophecy, as the Baptist was before his first comming. # Chapt. VII.

## *Against the fourth demonstration taken from the publike persecution.*

Your other ioint signe of Antichrists comming is a publike persecution, which you say, *shalbe most greiuous and notorious*, so as all publike Ceremonies, and Sacrifices of Religions shall cease, none of vvhich things vve see yet fulfilled, as you say, according ther- fore to the threefold note of this persecution, you set downe a three-fold proofe. First that it *shalbe most greiuous*. Secondly, that it *shall be most notorious*. Thirdly, *that all publike Religion shalbe made to cease* by meanes thereof. Novve you proue it shalbe most greiuous out of *Math. 24. 21. There shall then be a great Tribulation, such as vvas not from the beginning of the vvorld, nor shalbe*, and out of *Reuelat. 20. 3.* Where we reade, *that Satan shall then be loosed, vvho vvas bound vntill that time*, and this you confirme by the testimonies of *S. Austin, Booke 20. Chapt. 8. 9. Of the Citty of God; of Hippolitus the Martyr, and of Cyrill*, to which you adde in the ende, *that the Persecution by the Pope, is not the most greiuous; and therfore that he is not Antichrist*. I answere to each of these, & first as touching the greiouousnes of the persecution out of the words of Mathew, I saye that you care not a iot what you bringe to confirme your points withall, but you cite Scriptures hand ouer head. is uncertaine that the pestilence is the pestilence, because it is not ma-
nifest unto al men, whence it came at first, or that a fire upon an house
or Towne, is such a thing, and doth consume and deuoure all things
with the rage of it, because it is not so well discerned, and made
knowne, howe it began at first, and where, and by what degrees it
proceeded to such violence; But howsoeuer these things haue bene
perhaps somewhat like a riddle before this, yet nowe see howe much
we haue profited by that understanding, which God hath geuen us of
this heauenly book of the Reuelation, by the helpe whereof, we haue
touched neere uppon that first beginning of this pestilence and consu-
ming fire of the world, which you aske after. For we haue learnt
from hence, that presently after that the heathen Emperours were
discarded, the woman fled into the wildernes, and the burning Moun-
taine was cast into the Sea; Chapt. 12. and 8. For then did the ambi-
tion of the Romane Bishops breake asunder the barres and bounds
of humility, and sobriety, not enduring to be kept in any longer, then
began errours and superstitions of all forts to flye into the Church
swiftly, then was the Feast of the crosses finding out ordained & then
was confirmation made a newe Sacrament, and that of greater ho-
nour, then Baptisme it selfe, as it was Pope Miltiades his pleasure to
make it.
      Then euery one of the Bishops as they followed next in or-
der, laboured as it were for a wages to adde newe bastardly rites to
helpe to make up the full heape, till at length they came to see the
bottomlesse Pitt opened, when as the whole fogge brake forth, that
steamed out of hel it selfe.

## Chapt. VIII.

### *Against the fifth demonstration taken from*
### *the continuance of Antichrists raigne.*

You drawe your fifth demonftration from the continuance of Antichrifts raigne, vvhich you hold to be for three yeares and an halfe onely. *But feeing the Pope(fay you) hath raigned fpiritually in the Church novve for the fpace of 1500.yeares, and there can none be geuen that hath bene taken for Antichrift,vvho hath raigned precifely three yeares and an halfe;the Pope therefore is not Antichrift, and therfore Antichrift is not yet come.* I anfvvere, that I haue already fhewed by moft ftrong arguments taken out of the Scriptures, *howe brainfick an opinion this is of Antichrift of three yeares lafting and an halfe.* For if he haue raigned from the time of Conftantine the great, till this daye, vvhich this Booke of the Reuelation hath demonftrated vnto vs fo clearely as noe Iefuite fhall euer be able to pull vp vvhat vve haue planted thereout, it follovveth that *nothing is more fenfeleffe,then to conceite a kingdome that fhall laft but three yeares, and an halfe.* But the proper argument to proue this point is to be taken out of thofe things that follovve in the 20.Chap.4.5.verfes of this booke, vvhence it is plainely gathered, that one part of his Kingdome lafteth a thoufand yeares; For fo he faith, *And I favve the foules of them,vvho vvere fmit-ten vvith the fvvord for the teftimony of Iefus,and for the vvord of God,and vvho did not adore the beaft, nor his Image,nor tooke his marke in their for-heads,nor in their hands,and they liued and raigned vvith Chrift a thoufand yeares,but the reft of the dead men did not liue againe,till the thoufand yea-res vvere expired. ## Chapt. 9.

### Against the sixth Demonstration taken from the consummation of the World.

Your Sixth demonstration is taken out of the last Signe, that followeth after Antichrist, which shalbe the cōsummatiō of the World, thus. 
> *If Antichrist (saye You) had bene come long agoe, the World should haue bene ended longe since also; for he is to come a little before the ende of the World. But the vvorld is not yet ended, and therefore he is not yet come.*

The Consummation of the world may perhaps teach vs the ende of Antichrist, but it availeth nothing at all to demonstrate his coming if we will speake properly of him. This place is applied with one consent of all men as I suppose, to the last iudgement of our Lord: But this Booke of the Reuelation; teacheth vs both to thinke, and to speake more distinctly of this matter; For hence we doe vnderstand, that there is a double comming of the Lord yet to come, one Spirituall and that in an excellency; at the calling of the Iewes, another corporall, at the generall iudgement.

<header>Chap. 9. AGAINST BELLARMINE,</header>

Nowe that coming spoken of in Mathewe seemeth to be spirituall, which yet is described to be most glorious & powerfull with a bodily setting forth, both because it shalbe a most evident resemblance thereof and a certaine pledge as it were , as also there shall no change come afterwards betwene these two cōmings, that shall make the bodily to appeare like a newe one in respect of the former.

And we shall easily perceive that the matter is so as I saye, if we shal cōsider that the Disciples did inquire in the beginning of the Chapter touching the ende of the Temple, the comming of the Lord, and the ende of the world. Out of all doubt they comprehended the restoring of their nation under the comming of Christ, and therefore thinking that this coming of which he had put them in hope was at the resurrection of the Lord, they aske him afresh, 
> *Lord, wilt thou restore the Kingdome to Israel at this time, Act. 1. 6.*

But Christ answering them, and handling things that were to come in a continued order, first teacheth them about the destruction of Ierusalem, and the shattering of the Iewish people, and then he goeth on to enforme them about the rest of the course of matters, neither doth he make mention of any restoring in any place, before this glorious comming of his. Therefore either it must be contained in this apparition of his, or there must be none at all; which opinion had the Disciples cōceaued in their minds, and gathered it out of this answere of Christs, certainly they would not haue nourished in their minds any expectation of a Kingdome afterwards. Besides a tribulation goeth next before this comming, for so he saith, 
> *straight after the tribulation of those dayes, the sunne shalbe darkened, and then shall the signe of the Sonne of man appeare, &c.*

But there shall no such Tribulation as this goe immediatly before the corporal comming: For after the Iewes are called, and a newe Church is made, God will wipe away all teares, from their eyes, & there shalbe no more death, nor mourning, nor crying, nor greife, because the things that went before are gone awaye, Reuel. 21. 4. Wherefore that comming is not corporall. Perhaps also those words haue some force in them to proue this, where he saith, *that the signe of the Sonne of man shall appeare*, as if he would distinguish betwene this spirituall comming of his; and that other that was to followe. this similitude is fit enough to expresse that thing which the Apostle
meaneth. For the beames of the Sunne & the Sunne it selfe are beheld
alwayes at the same houre; so that he who make all this last age but
one houre, did not doe amisse to place the forerunners thereof in the
beginning of it. But as for you who make the last houre to be three
yeares and an halfe, what helpe can you haue from the similitude of
the Sunne and his beames? For though you deuide the houre into

howe unlike are his ministers to the beames of the sunne? the beames

## Chapt. X.

->Of the proper name of Antichrist.<-

Nowe we are come to your fourth heade of this Controuersy, which hath two questions in it to dispute of, one touching the proper name of Antichrist, and the other about his Marke. His proper name is gathered by one consent of all writers, out of that nomber of his name that is spoken of chapt. 13. 18. And his nomber is 666. nowe we haue shewed vppon that place, that this name is no other but (Latinos) seing experience confirmeth it most plainly, together with the agreement of all matters. And indeed Ireneus hath written many Ages agoe, that this name is very likely to belong to him, how he was moued so to write, whether it were by his owne cōiecture or whether he had receaued it of others, who were perhaps the Apostles schollers, his words are these touching this matter. *But the name (Latinos) also, containeth the nomber of 666; and is very likely because the truest Kingdome that is hath this name for they are the Latines, that doe nowe raigne; but vve vvill not sett vp our rest of this name.* These things saith he; I cōfesse that Ireneus doth not rest in this name, and that he doth thinke Teitan to be more worthy of credit; but yet he came neerer the marke then he was aware with his cōiecture touching the Latine kingdom; now because

### Chapt. XI.

->*Of the marke of Antichrist.*<-

WE haue declared abundantly Chapter 13. 16. 17. in what things the Marke of the Beast cõsisteth, against which Bellarmine obiecteth two things ; one out of the Text, another out of the antiquity of the signes, wherein we place and bound the Marke. He gathereth foure things out of the Text. *First that the marke shalbe one, and not many ; For saith he, the Scripture doth alvvayes speake in the singular nomber, as vvel of the Character, as of the name, and the nomber of the name of Antichrist, & therefore seing the aduersaries multiply so many Characters, as the Character, the preistly anointing, the profession of the Romish faith, &c. they knowe not vvhat this Marke should be. I answere that that is very weake which you saye touching the singular nomber of the Character, seing Aretas, Complutensis, and some other Coppies of no small authority reade it thus in the 6. verse, that they may geue marke vnto them, neither doe they meane many mar- kes in regard of the multitudes of them that doe take the marke, seing the same Coppies doe with one consent expresse the Seale of God in the singular nomber, though they speake of many, as vvhich haue not the seale not the seales, Chapter 9. 4. Besides is it strange to you to haue many things signified by a singular nomber, and on the contrary to haue one thinge expressed by a plurall nomber? But the name and the nomber of the name are singular matters, be it so ; Certainly you might aswell conclude that Mizraim is in the singular nomber, because Put and Canaan with whome it is ioined, are in the same nõber, Gen. 10. 6. Who was euer so strict as to require this, that all words which are reckoned vp in some sentence should be alike in all things, case, nomber, or Gender? or if Grammarrules wil not satisfye you, Logick will make you be quiet, which teacheth that a Character is one in name, many in deed. ## Chapt. XIII.

### Of Antichrists Seate.

In expounding the words of this Prophecye, we haue concluded it withmost strong arguments taken from thence, that Rome is the Seate of Antichrist; and that straightwayes after that the Empire was taken away from the heathen Emperours. For the heads of the Beast remaine at Rome, where both those hilles, and kings are which the Angell speaketh of. But where these heads remaine fixed, there must Antichrists seate needs be. More ouer seeing Antichrist was subsisting so soone as Constantine entred vpō his kingdomes as we haue proued before by many arguments, he hath had no other seate but at Rome. For in that he stayed at Auenion for a fewe yeares, he did that to soiourne there onely, not with a minde to change his seate. But you (o Bellarmine) fight on the contrary side, *holding that Ierusalem shalbe Antichrists seate, not Rome, the Temple of Salomon, and Throne of Dauid, not the Temple of S. Peter, and the Apostolike Chaire.* Which thing you endeauour to proue two wayes, first by an *Argument*; and then out of the *Scriptures*, and *Fathers*. The *Argument* stands thus.

> *If the Pope of Rome be Antichrist, sitting in the Church of Christ, then the Lutherans and Caluinists, and as many are strangers from that Church vvhich is vnder the Pope, keepe vvithout the true Church of Christ. For the Church of Christ cā be one onely, as Christ is one; but our men say you doe stand stiffely vppon it, that the Pope of Rome is Antichrist Therfore all our mē are banishēd avvay from the Church*

I answere that the Proposition is false, and that it doth relie onely vpō the peruerse vnderstāding of the vnity of the Church. For the Church is both commonly & properly so called. That is such a Church, as wherein piety is corrupted, the word is adulterated, the sacraments are depraued, that is full of superstition, and mens deuices; retaining onely the name of Christ, and boasting of the name thereof, as also which is so called commonly, as long as there is any part of the foundation left unshaken. ## Chapt. XIV.

### *Of Antichrists Doctrine.*

VVe teach and hold, & that out of the scriptures them selues, as
the Holy Ghost hath also taught vs out of them , that the
Doctrine of Antichrist, is full of hypocrisy, fraude, & crafty subtilties,
so that it may deceaue euē those that are otherwise most prudent men,

the Popes proctours stande vppon it, that this same Doctrine of An-
tichrist is so openly, impious & blasphemous , that no man can be so
blockish , but he must perceiue & detest it at the first hearing of it.

Doctrine of his to foure Heads: First that he shall deny Iesus to be Christ
& therefore that he shall labour to ouerthrowe all the ordinances of our sa-

## Chapt. XV.

### Of the Miracles of Antichriſt.

Touching the miracles of Antichriſt *there are as you ſay, three things ſett Downe in Scriptures ; Firſt , that he ſhould doe many meracles , ſecondly that they ſhould be lying miracles ; thirdly that there are three examples of miracles inſtanced in ;* in all which things I doe eaſily aſſent vnto you , but why doe you not ſhewe vs which all, that the Pope doth neither worke many miracles, nor lying miracles, nor any of thoſe three miracles that are by name mentioned, that ſo you might make it plaine, that the Pope is nothing a kin to antichriſt ? you ſeeme hereby to haue bene afraid of a iuſt trial, but feare or feare not, wil ye nil ye you & your Pope muſt be brought to your great Inqueſt about this Point ? Out of all doubt you neither can, deny neither haue you any liſt to deny it , that your Pope and antichriſt reſemble one an other notably like two twinnes, in working multitudes of miracles, ſeeing this is one of the principall Marckes by which your Church boaſts that ſhe is knowne to be the onely true Catholike Church. Wherefore there is no controuerſy about the firſt point; But let vs a litle examine the next point, and let vs ſee whether thoſe Miracles which haue bene wrought by the Popes, & their iourny men ſince the time that Antichriſt firſt began to ſhewe his head, be lying wonders or no, that ſo it may with all appeare whether our men doe ſlander you with a matter of truth or no. <header>OF THE APOCALYPSE. Chap. 18.</header>

<image-desc>A horizontal decorative band consisting of repeating ornamental fleurons separates the header from the chapter title.</image-desc>

## The 18. Chapter of the Reuelation.

### The logicall Resoluing.

*Hitherto we haue heard with and of what fashion the Throne of the Beast is; the describing whereof hath bene the first and a lighter sprinkling of the fifth Viall; nowe followeth a more plentifull pouring of it out, which is ioined with the ruine it selfe of this Throne. Which we distinguish into those things which goe before the ruine thereof, and those things which followe after. Those things are accomplished by the ministery of three Angels, two of which doe declare this destruction in bare words. The first is a glorious Angel, vers. 1. Who doth declare it more concisely, vers. 2. 3. The second Minister who hath no name, doth declare it more fully, first by exhorting the Godly both to flee out of Babylon, vers. 4. 5. As also by inciting those that were to be the instruments of this destruction, that they would vse due and deserued seuerity, vers. 6. 7. And then by describing, partly the bitter lamentation of the Wicked Kings, vers. 9. 10. Of the Wicked Merchants, vers. 11. 12. 13. 14. 15. 16. Of the Wicked oare men, and Mariners, vers. 17. 18. 19. Partly the ioye of the Godly, vers. 20. So much for the ministery of the two Angels. The third vseth a signe also besides his words, which is both propounded, vers. 21. and explaned, summarily in the same verse, particularly, vers. 22. 23. 24. Thus farre goe those things which goe before this ruine. That which followeth it, is a thanksgiving, which the Saints render vnto God for it, Chapt. 19. 1. 2. 3. 4.*

# THE EXPOSITION.

Verses. 1. *And after these things I savve an Angell descending*, We see he-
re howe God will make his admirable Patience to be manifest to all
the world, whē he goeth about the destruction of the Citty of Rome;
for besides all the former warnings that he had geuen it, which were
so many, and of so many kinds faire and foule, he doth not come dow-
ne to execute his last iudgement against it, but first he sendeth three
Angels, by whose voice mē might be admonished, to avoide the plague
that was rushing in vpon them. The first of these is, *an Angell comming
dovvne from heauen*, that is some exellent and worthy man, such an one
as should come sodainly, before he be looked for, as those things doe,
which flippe downe from heauen; Those things which spring vp
among vs earth, doe yeeld some shewe and signe of them sel-
ves, before they growe to their ripenes; but those that come from hea-
ven, can be vpon vs, and in the middest of vs in a moment, so as we cā
perceiue no foresight or fore knowledge of them afore-hand. So in
the 10 Chapt; *an Angell came dovvne from heauen*, when as many stout
Patrones of the truth arose on a sodaine, of which their was no suspi-
cion before. And this selfe same thing is confirmed by other places,
which may be fetched out of this Interpretation. This Angell seemeth
to be one that shall be sodainly conuerted to the Truth, who shall the-
reby make it manifest to all men, that he commeth downe from hea-
ven. Such was that descending in the tenth Chapter, where men that
had bene nousled long in superstition, were made the nurselings of the
truth and true piety on a sodaine. This *Angel hath great povver*; But to
what ende? For there is no worthy exploit of his spoken of; it may
be that this is he, to whose charge the demolishing of this Throne is
committed; who shall not so much bring a newe prophecy touching
the ruine of Babylon, as he shal shewe him selfe to be addressed to put
that matter in execution, which the Oracles of God had often fore-
told, that it should be.

Thirdly, *the earth vvas made bright vvith his glory*, because euen they
who are strangers from the true Church, shall honour & admire him

Vers. 6. *Reward her as she hath rewarded you.* The other part of the exhortation belongs to the armies of Souldiers which are to be mustered together against Rome, hereby he doth whet them on & set them on fire with indignatiõ against her, that so they might take vengeāce on her the more fiercely. To answere this, we knowe what the Lord saith; *Cursed is he that doth the worke of the Lord negligently.* Neither are we to feare that the punishment should be greater and more seuere then she had deserued; seeing no sharpenes & fiercenes of plagues could be equal to her horrible sinnes. Because God is a strong Lord. For if they ſhall bring final deſtruction vpon Rome with their forces vnited together, as the Ieſuite wil haue it, then they ſhould leaue no King to bewaile her calamity. We haue proued by more found arguments then this conceite ſtandeth on, that the ten Hornes belong to the onely ranke of Emperours, ſome one of whom perhaps ſhal effect this ruine of Rome at length, who doth yet keepe the name of the whole number, as it is the vſual manner, when ſpeach is had about the members or parts of any whole. While this one King ſhall laye Rome waſt, ſome other of the Kings, as the Spaniſh King, the King of Polonia, and others of the like ſtraine, that are of the vnholy league with the whore, ſhall make this miſerable out alas and well adaye.

Verſ. 10. *Shall ſtand a farre of.* But what ſhould they ſtand weeping and wailing at this time? Why wil they not make haſt rather to come and helpe her? They ſhal not dare for feare; for they ſhalbe in a very bodily feare in regard of their owne ſafety, which ſhall now ſeeme to be in danger. They ſhall therfore behold her miſery a farre of, fearing leaſt that if they ſhould come neerer, they the ſelues ſhall be burnt vp with the ſame fire. Nowe therfore ô you Holy & Chriſtian Princes, ſet vppon this worthy and heroical exploite at length. It will not be ſo hard and troubleſome a buſines as you take it perhaps. Verf. 12. *The vvares of Gold and siluer.* We said right nowe that this whole Allegory is taken out of Ezech. 27. Where speach is had about the Destruction of Tyrus. And that not vnvvorthily, as vve haue shewed at the .3 verse, seeing Rome is no lesse infamous for merchandizing of foules, then Tyrus vvas famous for marting of Bodily Vterfills. Ezechiel doth reckon vp each of the Nations in such fort, that he doth vvith all sett downe by name the proper commodities of each Country, vvith vvhich both they abounded them selues, and they made Tyrns to aboūd vvith them also by carrying them out thether for traffick : According to this consideracon, the sundry kinds of vvares seeme to be reckoned vp in this place, that they might note out vvnto vs the sundry nations, to vvhich either they doe properly belong, or at least by vvhose trauaile and paines they are conueyed to Rome. Therefore though the names of the cuntries are not set downe expressely, as they be in Ezechiel, yet they may be easily vnderstood by the vares them selues, according to that rule. The vvares therefore of siluer and Gold and of the rest of the outlandish commodities vvhich are spoken of in this verse, maye signifie spaine, vvhich fetched these things out of the furdest parts of the Indian cuntries; & by vvhose meanes they are made saleable in this part of the vvorld. Vvhere vve liue, *cinnamon, odours, ointments, frankincense, & vvine*, note Italy out, not because euery one of these things growe there, but because as spaine transporteth these things into Europe, by meanes of the Ocean, so Italy affordeth Europe plenty of these things, vvhich it fetched out of Grecia, Cilicia, Arabia, Egypt by an invvard fea; and besides It selfe doth most abound vvith all kinds of fuch delightfull fruites as these be, of all the Countries in Europe. *Fine floure, and vvheate* may note out the Iles of the invvard sea, Sicilia & sardinia, vvhich be the garners, and victualing storehouses of Italy. *Beasts* signifie Germany that is full of them, Euen as sheepe may expresse our Country of England, vvhich is most famous of all other for that kinde of cattell; *Horses and charets* note out the French men, vvho haue great plenty of Horses, and from vvhome this vse of Charretts & such kinde of conueiance hath bene deriued ouer other cnntries; *Bodies* doe expresse the swizers, vvho liue by exercising their bodies in an outvvard vvarfare for hire and paye, and vvhich are commonly retained by the Pope of Rome, to be the principall of his gard next vvnto his proper person. *The Soules of men* are the common vvares of all Cuntries vvhich

lost al their hope of Gaine, which is the onely thing that makes these

*Shall stand alofe of.* Namely the Cardinals, the Bishops, & others

Gunshott, shall yet bewaile *Romes* ruine with a lamentable voice,
standing aloofe of and looking on, but they shal neither haue hornes
nor hart strong enough to driue away iminent dangers.

Verſ. 18. *What Citty vvas like to this great one ?* Thus doe mari-
ners cry touching Tyrus, Ezech. 27. 32. *What Citty vvas equall to Tyrus,
that is cutt dovvne in the midft of the Sea?* And they had caufe thus to be
aftoniſhed at this, and to aſke this queſtion, ſeeing they conſidered of
the former wealthines of that Citty , which flouriſhed ere whiles by
meanes of that entercourſe of merchandize which it had with ſo
many & ſo great Nations ; ſo that they thought it to be vnconquerable
by any ſtrēght of man. What a deale of trouble did it putt Nabuchad-
nezzar to ? Ezech. 29. 18. Howe greatly was Alexander the great
pufled in beſeiging it after wards ? For he was ſo out of hope to ouer-
come & to ouerthrow it, that he repented that he had begun the Seige
againſt it, & yet he neuer thought any other thing els to hard for him.
But theſe mariners & watermen ſhall be aftoniſhed farre more iuſtly
with meruailing at Rome, that had bene the Queene of all the world
many ages ſince ; that had bene called the moſt ancient Citty, the Chaire of
Peter, *vvhich vvas alvvayes more inuincible, thē that ſhe could be ouerthrovvne
vvith any calamities, vvhich ſhould alſo continue exceeding mighty & flouri-
ſhing both vvith her ovvne & her frends vvealth and great eftate, & that euen
to her crooked Age, and dying daye ;* These and many ſuch things more,
will make them to crye out and to ſaye, *What Citty is like to this great
one ?* who would not haue beleeued , that ſuch an excellency that was ſo
eminent in all reſpects , ſhould be free from all decay & deſtruction ?
Howe groſſely haue we bene deceaued that haue dreamed of her Eter-
nity ? & howe lewdly we deceaued others, whē we in our preachings
auouched ſo confidently , that this Ship of ours ſhould neuer be drow-
ned. Howe vnexpected haue all these things bene beyond all that euer
we haue beleeued, imagined, or boaſted. Of this is the force of this
queſtion that is ſo ful of amazednes.

Verſ. 19. *And they ſhall caft duft on their heads.* After the man-
ner of mourners ; Iob. 2. 12. For these ſhall mourne the more earneſt-
ly, by howe much leſſe able they ſhalbe to ſuſtaine them ſelues by their
owne wealth. But the Angell ſpeakes here in the time paſt, *they haue
caft duft, and they did cry,* & in the former verſe, *they did crye vvhen they
ſavve the ſmoke.* And yet these things goe before the ruine of Rome, as
which followeth next in order and immediatly after. For which cauſe
hee ſeemeth to change the tenſe , and not onely becauſe of the moſt
certaine truth of the matter that is to come, as the Prophets are wont
to ſpeake elſewhere.

Where in all are become rich. Not onely those Purpled Fathers , but
euen the basest Swabber in the Shipp. I Take a viewe of the whole

their Share. Yea and which is meruailous strange to be spoken , those
that made shew as if they could not vphould their poore estate ,but by
begging from Doore to Doore,in the streets , wanted nothing that
might serue euen to make them liue in riott and excesse. So miserable
was the common people euery where , that was gulled so by these
cheating knaues , that they laid out their money vppon beggars that
were wealthier then they them selues who gaue the Almes.

But so great skill hath Rome to enrich her followers;Those runna-

are they entertained at Rome,in Spaine,& in other Popish places?They
get that in forraine Cuntries for a reward of their Treasõ, which they
could not come by at home in the waye of honesty. There wanteth
nothing at home to reward those that doe well,but these night-owles
hate the light of true virtue,and yet they would haue al that that is due
vnto it. These are the fellowes, whome Rome maketh rich, counting
it a foule shame for her selfe (so Godly a heart would this vngracious

glory, should not waxe rich by meanes of her abundance alone that

Vers. 20. *O heauen reioice ouer her.* Thus farre goeth the mourning of the wicked ; Nowe the Holy Ghost sheweth howe great and abundant ioye shal accrue to the Godly from the Fal of Rome. Heauen is the vniuersall multitude of the Saints on earth ; as we haue often obserued. Apostles and Prophets in this place are not those famous Preachers of the truth of God, and founders of the Churches, which were subsisting on earth in ancient times, but all the Godly men , that shall be then liuing , and discharging the function of Teachers in the Church. For what doe our matters on earth, belong to these holy blessed Soules that are and haue bene resting so long and so happily in the heauens? dead men (saith the wise Salomon) knowe nothing any more, nothing of our matters who are liuing as Pilgrimes & are absent from the Lord ; Ecclesiast. 9.5. And therefore the Prophet saith , *That Abraham is ignorant of vs, and that Israel knoweth vs not*, Esay 63.16. Therefore they are the holy Teachers that are and shalbe liuing vppon the earth, whome the Holy Ghost calleth Apostles and Prophets in this place, and that for this ende , that they might be comforted by this name here geuen them against those troubles and vexations , which they finde and meete with in and from the world that though they be inferiour by many degrees to the Apostles so old in gifts & graces yet they should knowe that they are in account and estimation with God, as if they were Apostles and Prophets. He calleth vpon these by name, because their ioye shalbe the chiefest, as thier misery and distresse haue bene greatest, because the whore hath burnt out with more deadly hatred against them, then against any other degree of men. Out of which we perceiue that which we spake of before, that seeing this ioye is common to all the Elect, that those mourning merchants spoken of verse 11. are not among this blessed company, and therefore that they are called merchants rather because they resemble them, then because they are such in truth.

For God hath punished her. The Hebrue manner of speaking which is expressed in the Greeke is more significant, according to which the words goe thus, *because God hath iudged your iudgement vppon her*; This kind of speach signifieth punishment, but such as is not inflicted, rashly but vppon iust and lawfull examination, conuiction and iudgement going before. shewed by probable reason that it shalbe besieged for some time ; for so old Babylon was not subdued by Cyrus & brought into his power, till after some long delaye, but therefore is this thus deliuered, because the laying of Rome wast shalbe most quickly at an ende , after that it shalbe once taken, and shalbe begun to be spoiled. Verse. 22. *And the voice of harpers* : He Openeth this ruine of Rome in more words, after the manner of the Prophets, who are wōt to describe the vtter destructiō of any place with such kinde of words; as Ierem.25.10.

He meaneth that all things shall perish which pertaine either to their present delight , or necessity, or els to their future encreasing & multiplying vppon earth. For this especial nōbring vp of matters serueth to teach vs thus much. They are called Harpers which sing and play on their harpes; They are called Musicians with a common name, that sing with a loud voice. The Pipe and Trumpet are Wind-instruments; the one hauing a softer and sweeter sound , the other hauing a more harsh and terrible sound, fitt for warre , and yet there is some use of it at solemne meetings in time of peace. But they are all brought in to expresse the ioye and iollity which Rome liued in, as we learn out of Ieremy, from whome these words are taken, so that it were against learning yea reason it selfe and the scope of this place, to make a long talke about Pipes used at funerals, as the Iesuites doth in this place. *And no Craftsman*. After those things that belong to expresse that which helpeth to nourish & testify thier voluptuous life, he cometh to speake of those things which come more neere to expresse that which helpes to keepe life & soule together; of which kinde of matters, there is more neccessary use, such as artificers, and milles be. ## *The 19. Chapter.*

### The Resoluing there of into the seuerall Contents.

Thus *farre haue those things bene handled which goe before, or are ioined together with the Ruine of* Rome, *nowe followeth that which cometh after it; And that is a thanksgiving to* God *in the foure first verses, and that two fold, one of the confused multitude both at first geuen to* God *for taking iust vengeance uppon the whore, vers. 1. 2. As also repeated againe, because of the eternity of the same punishment, vs. 3. The other of the* Elders, *&* *of the* Beasts, *vers. 4. And so much of the more full explaning of the fifth* Viall. *There are two yet remaining; the sixth to be poured out uppon* Euphrates, *and the seauenth uppon the* Aire. *That former is handled in the rest of this Chapter, on to the 20. verse. This is continued from thence to the conclusion of the whole Booke; There were two parts of that former viall set downe* Chap. 16. *The drying up of* Euphrates, *and a* Preparation *to* A Battell. *In like manner we haue two parts of the explaning thereof laid downe. We shewed that that drying up of* Euphrates *doth note out unto us the calling of the* Iewes, *which is described in this place first by an inuitemēt to praise* God, *vers. 5. And by the ioye of the frends compainons of the* Bride, *vers. 6. 7. As also by a preparation to the marriage vs. 8. After that by the certainty of the thinge it selfe, which he therefore*

## THE EXPOSITION.

After these things I heard a voice In resoluing of this Chapter we referre these foure first verses to the Fifth Viall , that is , to the Fall of Rome . As wherein we are taught what ioyfull matter of praising God the destruction of Rome shall affoord to the saints . The Angel exhorted them to reioice aboue chap. 18.20. Nowe therefore whē the matter is once accomplished, all the Godly shall triumph in good earnest, & with all their hearts. But seing this exceeding ioye of theirs followeth the fal of Rome, it must needs be that , either that casting of the Milstone into the sea is the destroying of the Cittye, or els, that māner of the destruction there of, is altogether concealed ; which yet shall happen betwene that signe and this Thanksgiving. The first Gratulation is *of a great multitude in heauen*, that is, of a confused company of all sorts of People that shall then be conuersing in the Church vppō Earth. For we abidestill in the signification of this word that is vsuall in this booke, which will not suffer vs to referre these things here spoken of to any knowledge that the heauēly soules haue of matters that are done vppon earth. The Cittizens therefore of the Church militant that are abiding in any place of the world whether the Report of Romes ruine shalbe rumoured , shall leape for the excessiue ioye they cōceiue, & by meanes thereof they shall breake forth into this thankful acknowledgement of Gods goodnes to his Church in Punishing Rome.

Halleluia. This is an Hebrue word , signifying *Praise ye the Lord*, whereby the faithfull doe prouoke one another to geue thankes vnto God, and they cheare vp their hearts and Tune their spirits to performe this duety in the best manner , by making this Preface as it were there vnto. True ioye of the Holy Ghost, will not endure to be kept & Cowped vp in any one mans breast and bosome, but it striueth to gett companions : both for the pouring out & imparting of it selfe vnto them, that they may be filled and refreshed out of this spring of ioye; as also that it selfe may be the more increased and inflamed by this ioint reioicing of many good hearts together , that are all baptised into one Spirit,

Spirit, and are there by made able one to inflame and to edifie another. This one word containeth in it a large Theme, to make abundance of ioyfull matter on . But why doth this heauenly Hoſt ſpeake Hebrue at this time ? what ? is there ſome more holines and myſtery lying vnder concauities of theſe Letters and ſyllables , then if they were words of another Tongue ? Theſe be the Toyes and deuices of our Rhemiſh Tranſlatours. Are then theſe & ſuch like Hebrue words as *Oſanna* *Amen*, *Abba* & the like retained in the Greeke and other Tranſlations, for this ende that we might make vſe of them to be ſignes and remẽbrances vnto vs as it were of our coniunction with Holy Church that was in the old Lawe before Chriſt , namely that we doe both beleeue in one and the ſame God and that we doe call vpon him alone ? This is indeed a profitable vſe that we may make , of theſe words thus retained and a good reaſon why they are retained, but it ſeemeth that the chiefe cauſe why they are retained in this place is , becauſe the Church of the Gentiles , ſhall prouoke their brethren the Iewes , to Embrace the faith of Chriſt , after that Rome ſhalbe once deſtroyed ſeeing that maine impediment ſhalbe then taken away , which did moſt mightily barre vp the waye from their conuerſion. For it was not Poſſible that the People that crucified the Lord ſhould acknowledge him to be their Lord , as long as Rome flouriſhed , yea or had any being in the world, as which was the Place that gaue them power and authority to crucifie him. This is the cauſe why this Hebrue word is ſo often refounded and rung out againe and againe in this place : Theſe Praiſes that were geuẽ to God beefore in this booke were not expreſſed in theſe words; but ſeeing the conuerſion of the Iewes is ioined next vnto this Gratulation, the ſaints doe nowe vppon great reaſon ſpeake in laugnage of the Iewes, as with whome they deſire to be made one Sheepfold, & to ſpeake the language of Canaan.

Saluation & honour & glory that is , Praiſe honour and glory to be geuen vnto our Lord for fhewiug forth his mercy & power in ſauing vs and in deſtroying our enemies. Glory is a certaine high opinion which one hath of a mans excellency for which cauſe it hath the name in Greeke, *Idia doxa* , wherefore in this deſtruction of Rome there ſhall ſhine forth ſo bright a Beame of Gods goodnes & power , that all faithfull men ſhall meruaile and be amazed at it. Honour is that worſhip as well inward as outward, whereby we doe reuerence and

**Vers. 2.** *For true and righteous.* This truth in iudgements respec-
teth the promise of God; Iustice respecteth the punishing of the eni-
mies according to his promise; & their deserts. The faith in both these 
Attributs of God was vtterly perished amōg the wicked of the world,

for both these respects, seeing he should now make the world to kno-
we and trye ynough and more too, (as they would nowe thinke) that 
God is an auenger of wickednes, and that he doth not alwayes winke 
at the wrongs that are offered vnto his People.

**Verse. 3.** *And againe they said.* Here is another Thanksgiving: 
expressed, which shalbe made after that the matter is more certainly 
knowen to be true & certaine. The first messenger that brings the first 
newes that the Citty is takē, shall poure forth the first Praises of God: 
But when as once the faithfull shall haue heard that Rome is vtterly 
rased Downe to the ground, with out any hope of restoring and rene-
wing againe, they shall renewe their Ioye, and with all they shall sing 
newe sōgs of Praise to God which they shal poure out of their fresh-
springs of hearty ioye. The second Gratulation is expressed in fewer 
words then the former, perhaps it is recorded so shortly, to make vs 
see the dul disposition of our nature, who at the first onset of a matter 
are fire and towe, but we waxe coole inough & to much afterwards.

*And the smoke thereof Rose vp.* That is, nowe is Rome deliuered vp 
to be tormented euerlastingly. For euerlasting fire and torments are 
declared by the rising vp for euer more; by which kinde of speach we 
are taught, that the perpetuall remembrance of that punishment, shall 
be alwayes worthily magnified of all the Godly, as who should haue 
the signe thereof, (this smoke alwayes ascending) euer and anon ex-
posed to their sight least perhaps it might be buried in forgetfullnes. 
Here is an allusiō made to the euerlasting torments which the wicked 
shall endure. Therefore this Eternity of the Punishment that shall fall

So *Psal.* 110:3. *Thy people shall come most vvillingly of all other in the daye of thy armies, vvith the Holy beauties, out of the vvombe of morning, the devve of thy youth shall come vnto the* Many such places of Scripture might be brought to this purpose, and perhaps it would be profitable to bring them, at least for this ende that our writers might haue occasion thereby geuen them, to consider more diligently of these places, from the right interpretation whereof I feare me, that we wander. when as we make them to speake of things that be past, nowe whereas they doe foretell of things yet to come. This sentence therefore which is commanded to be written, takes away al Scruple from Iohn; He might haue thought on the former obstinacy of this Iewish Nation, and might haue doubted of their conuersion in that regard.

But the Angel biddeth him cast away this care and feare, and telleth him that this people shalbe so greatly willing and desirous to come, that it shall suffice onely to haue called them. It is to be obserued, that the Iewes are here and elsewhere commonly, said to be men that haue bene called, for so is the participle here put in the preter perfect tense, as also *Math.* 22.3.4.8. When it is applied to the Iewes; And hereby a certaine prerogatiue seemeth to be noted, which the Iewes haue before others in their calling, as who haue bene called from the first beginning of the world. But the Gentiles are said to be men that are called, in the present tense, because they were first called at the comming of Christ, or rather from the time of his death. And this difference seemeth to be obserued in this Reuelation also, whereupon those who are said to subdue the ten Kings, hauing the Lambe for their Captaine, are called those that are called, and chosen, who as it is certaine, are the faithfull among the Gentiles.

But the naturall placing of the wordes as they lie in the greeke hath great force in it , which is lost if they be transposed, thus; These true words, are are the wordes euē of God him selfe, that is, they continue in them a most diuine, excellent, & certain Truth. For some words of a man also are true, but the truest words we speake haue some infirmities lying vnder them. We alwaies speake out of the earth, Iohn. 3. 31. There is therefore a kinde of excellence geuen to this Truth, which appeareth not, if we change the order of the words. It is no strāge matter to say, that the words of God are true.

*Vers. 10. And I fell before his feete* Why doth he fall downe now, more then before time? what was he smitten with the Maiesty of the Angel? This meruailous Vision is seene in heauen that is opened, that is, in the holy Church, whose most renowned and glistering glory, shalbe nowe made most manifest vnto all men, as aboue the notable dignity and excellency of the first Church, of the Gentiles, such as it was to be seene in the times of the Apostles, and straight after, was signified by the doore opened in the heauen; Chapt. 4. 1. Vers. 17. *Then I sawe a certaine Angel standing in the Sunne.* Thus farre goeth the description of the Captaine ; nowe the Holy Ghost commeth to describe certaine of the Souldiers, that must encounter with the Beast. That other shal sound an Alarum to the battel,by stirring vp the Saints thereunto.Neither shal he that poureth out the Vial stand in the Sunne it selfe,but being seated some where els,he shall cast abroad his liquor vppon it. This Angel as it were sitting downe in the Charret of Phæbus , takes vp his standing with in the Compasse of that great light.But wil some man say,howe shal we be able to conceiue euen in our thoughts of any such thing as this ? I thinke that we may fetch a light to finde out this Sunne here meant, out of Chapt. 12. 1. Where we heard that the woman was clothed with the Sunne, that is , that she glittered on euery side round about , with the most cleare light of the Scriptures, with the cleare knowledge whereof she being adorned as it were with a goodly garment , came forth abroad,and layd her selfe open to the viewe of the world. Nowe one may be said to stand in his clothing , as the Spouse standeth at the Kings right hand in Gold of Ophir, *Pfal.45.10.* This Angel therefore shalbe some cittizen of that particular Church, which shall shine forth most gloriously,with honour and renowme,aboue the rest by meanes of her witnessing vnto, and mainteining of the most Holy Truth in a special manner , whereby she shall approue her selfe to be the natural daughter of that woman that is clothed with the Sunne. We knowe that there is not the same purity of al the particular Churches,which professe Christ,but that one drinketh in more dregges, & traileth more baggage stuffe after it then another.But this Angel shal be a member of that most intire and most chast congregation of al the rest,which shal be most glistring,and gorgeous of al the rest,by meanes of this glorious araye. Saying to all the foules vvhich did flie by the middst of heauen. We haue obserued before. Chapt. 8. 13. & 14. 6. That the word in the Greeke translated, the middle of heauen, signifieth place betvvene heauen & earth, as it were the midle Regiõ of the Aire where Meteores are ingendred, and that it doth not signifie the middest of heauen in the length of it which the Astronomers call Meridies, the point where the Sunne is at Noone-daye; and therfore that this worde serueth to decypher out vnto vs, the imperfect perfection, and the impure Purity of those men, who haue escaped out of the horrible filthines of grosse superstition by the knowledge and acknowledging of the truth, and yet they haue not attained to such Purity, as was meete for those that dwel in heauẽ. The Angell of the sunne calleth all these to take part in diuiding the spoile, as who are all of them the Schollers and foster-children of the same truth, howesoeuer it flourisheth not alike among them all, in equall sanctimony, and integrity. Out of which we vnderstande, that howesoeuer one or two, or some fewe of the congregations, shal professe and practise sincere piety, at the time when this warre shalbe waged with the Beast, yet the most of them, euen of those that are of reformed Religion, shalbe found such, as either neuer haue attained to full amendment of things that be amisse, or els they haue thoroughly their owne negligẽce, and carelefnes, fallen so farre backe againe, that they come farre short of the holines of a pure and vndefiled spouse.

And who seeth not that this declining and decaying takes place euery daye more and more throughout the Churches? There are some peruerse and refratary men, who will not be persuaded though they be persuaded, conuinced at least, that there is any such difference of Churches at this daye, as this that we speake of, and finde in this place and others; but yet those to whome God giueth this grace, to deny their owne wicked lusts, and imaginacions and to subiect them selues with all their thoughts, and iudgements, to be measured and directed by the onely square and Platforme of all truth, the perfect lawe of God, these humble & gracious men (I saye) that doe thus declare them selues feare God truly, doe both see, and with greife of heart they do bewaile it that there are many of those that should stand in the Sunne

things doe make this opinion probable. But notwithstanding, seeing
*Ezechiel* with whose prophecy this whole place, that was wholy taken
from thence, doth agree altogether, maketh this *Gog* the cheife
Prince and commander of *Meshech*, and *Tuball*, Chapt. 38.3. That
is, of the *Cappadocians*, and the *Iberians* in *Asia*, as *Iosephus* saith in
the 1. Booke of *Antiquit.* Chapt. 7. And there was none of *Gyges*
posteritye, no not *Craesus* who raigned last and furdest of them al, that
was euer Prince of these nations , as whose dominion was bounded
with in the precincts of the Riuer *Halys*, as *Herodotus* writeth in *Clio*,
there is therfore perhaps some other reason of this name. And it
seemeth to be this, that *Gog* should not be the vsuall name of any
Cuntry, but a name made of *Magog* , both that it might note out
the exceeding neere concord and amity of both these Nations ,
as also that it might appeare that *Gog* had his originall from
*Magog*.

But will some say what neerenes or affinity hath Gog with Magog, if we doe acknowledge him to be a Scythian in his beginning? It is very great both for stocke and nature. For Magog is a Scythian, and the Prince of that nation, as Iosephus saith antiquit. book 1. Chapt. 6. Magog (saith he) was the author of the Magogites who had their denomination from him, and are called scythians by the Greeke writers. I but sibylla seemeth to sing us another mãner of song, in her Description of the place where Magog was seated; when she saith;

> *vvoe vvoe vnto thee o cuntry of Gog, and thou Magog that are seated in the middest of the riuers of the æthiopians.*

Is Magog then amidst the riuers of the Ethiopians? we knowe that this Southrẽ People dwelleth nigh to the sea side; & that this name agreeth not to any nation, that is more neere unto the North, then unto Egypt; which is called Ethiopia many times, as Eustathius, teacheth uppon Dionysius. And this is that Ethiopia, doubtlesse, which sibylla understandeth, which she attributeth to Magog worthily. For who knoweth not, that the Cercasian Scythians were sent to inhabite in Egypt, where there is a Towne also called by their name Cercasorum. Besides Ezechiel nombreth the Persians, Ethiopians, and the men of Africa, whome he calleth Put, among the armies of Gog; chapt. 38. 5. Sibyll therefore doth not describe Magog by his owne Proper Cuntry, but by the Colony, whether he was sent; which he maketh mention of cheifely, because the Calamity of Magog should lie most heavy uppon that part of his Dominions. But be it that Magog is a scythian, howe did the Deuill seduce him? by stiring him vp to ioine his forces with the Turkes, and to endeuour to destroy the Christians together with them. When first newe troupes of the Scythians had broken in by the streights of the Caspian Sea, into that part of Asia that was nighe to them, which was about the yeare 1250. when Iohn Duca raigned at Nicea, they molested the Turkes that were of the same bloud with them, who came into those cuntries for some Ages before that. These they droue out of those Cuntries, beyond, Euphrates, into those streights of the lesser Armenia, and Cappadocia, which we spake of right nowe; so that they were compelled necessarily to entreat peace at the hands of the Romane Emperour, that they might be able to resist, the inuasions of the Scythians, that urged & pressed them at their backes.

And this stoode the state of matters with the Turkes , till the time appointed came, wherein the diuel should be loosed out of his chaines. But then being let goe out of his prison , he ended this controuersy betwene the Scythians and them , and wrought an vnity or rather a conspiracy of minds betwene them , so as they both agreed,to extinguish the Christian profession. From that time the Turke neuer wanted the helpe of the Scythians his countrimen ; vpon whose strength he much relyeth at this daye,as we sawe in the late warres against the Hungarians , wherein he had great forces of the Tartarians to helpe him,who are the naturall Scythians,the offspring of Magog.The combining therefore of Gog and Magog against the Saints,is openly seene at this daye;so as not any kinred,and neerenes of blood , but onely the fraud,and seducing of the Deuill hath made them confederates. And thus we see what this army of the Turkes and Scythians is , both of which people are of the same original,but the Turkes are called Gog, because they haue their offspring from Magog , as a riuer springeth from a Fountaine; although they be nowe the Principall commander in this warfare, neither doe they retaine any thing at al of the Scythians , by reason of the long staye which they haue made in Asia , but onely some footesteppe of the auncient name. But the Scythians partly those that came lately from thence, partly those that inhabite there at this daye,who yet are sent for into these Cuntries of Asia and the rest of the Turkes dominions , to aide them,as need requireth , are called by the name of their first founder and Gouernour.

The number of this Armye is infinite almost. *For it is like the sand by the Sea shore, that is, very huge and innumerable*, it was described before by a definite number , of *tvvo thousand times an hundred thousand* Chap.9.16. The forces of the Christians when they are all put together, doe scarce equal the fourth part of his armye in any Battel that is fought betweene them.

Last of all we maye perceaue his Taile with a longe traine swooping and trailing after him through Egypt, and the coast of Lybia, and as it were gathering it selfe into a rundell-or Circle. This serpẽt goeth not on with forth right paces, but wreathing him selfe into many hollowe windings, he thrusts his bodye forth & forward. Who is there that beholding this Empire, not so much stretching it selfe forth in length, as creeping with an oblique turning, may not perceiue a liuely Image of a crooked Serpẽt? I take no pleasure to catch butter-flies like children, that is, to let driue at sillye subtilties that haue no substance in them, but onely I desire to set before our eyes the truth as it seemeth to me of that Portraiture of a Serpẽt, which the holy Ghost hath deuised and described vnto vs.

Verf. 15. *And vvho foeuer vvas not found.* No man ſhalbe gathered into this Church, but he onely that ſhalbe among thoſe that haue bene choſen from euerlaſting, to eternall life. <header>chap. 21. A REVELATION,</header>

## The 21. Chapter.

### The Logicall Resoluing of it into the seuerall Contents.

<image-desc>Ornamental woodcut initial H featuring symmetrical botanical scrollwork and leafy motifs within a square border.</image-desc>
*Hetherto the Holy Ghost hath explaned the manner of gathering the Church together, after this the condition thereof is explaned, after that it shalbe once gathered; Which is declared to be most happy, first generally out of the things which are seene of Iohn, the Newe heauen and earth, vers. 1. and the Holy Cittye, vers. 2. as also out of the things which are heard of him Partly in common, touching the presence of God with men, verse 3. Touching the remouing of Calamities vers. 4. And a newe restoring of all things, vers. 5. Partly in priuate touching the Certainty of the Prophecy vers. 5. Touching the mysterye that was nowe fulfilled, vers. 6. & the rewarding both of the Godly, verse. 6. 7. As also of the wicked, verse 8. And so much for the generall opening of the happy estate of the Church. The particular opening of it relateth the cause that reuealeth it the Angel, vers. 9. 10. And the matter that is reuealed uniuersally Vers. 10. 11. seuerally in respect of the wall and the Citty and the essentiall parts thereof, as, of the forme of the wall, vers. 12. 13. 14. Of the Forme, of the Citty, vers. 15. 16. 17. And then of the matter, common, Vers. 18. of speciall, of the wall, vers. 19. 20. 21. Of the Citty, vers. 21. Eternall arguments, where with the glory of this Cittye is sett forth are first God him selfe, who is both the Temple, vers. 22, and the light of the Cittye, verse. 23. Secōdly the Nations, which shall bring their glory hether, vers. 24; which shalbe both voide of al feare & suspiciō, vers. 25. As also such as doth not defile it with any contagiō, vers. 27, Thirdly that meruailous abundance of things that are necessarily, and the Perpetuallnes of this glory; in the Chapter following.*

## THE EXPOSITION.

*And I favve a nevve heauen.* The opinion of the refurrection vvhich vvas grounded vppon the ende of the former Chapter, hath perfuaded very many mē, to interprete al thefe things of the Church, fuch as it is to be at lenght in the heauēs. But vve haue fhewed, that there is neither any fpeach had in that place, of the laſt refurrection, neither yet doth the Holy Ghoſt paint out vnto vs in this place the Angel-like happines of the Saints after this life, But that he is ſtill entreating of matters to be done vppon earth, as the matters them felues vvhich are ſpoken of, vvill make it manifeſt in their proper places. And perhaps vve may thinke that it vveere no needfull matter for vs, to haue the heauenly inheritance to be fett forth vvith vvords, as vvhich all men knowe fufficiently to be aboue all the praifes that can be giuen vnto it by any man; yea euen thoſe men knowe thus much, vvho are vvont othervvife to thinke bafely of the Church vppon earth, as if it vvere a vile and contemptible matter. But the eftimation of the Church as it is a pilgrime on earth, is leffe then it ought to be among mortall men; fo that there might be a neceffary reafon, vvhy the glory and dignity thereof ſhould be more plentifully commended. And yet the defcription thereof, giueth vs a good Rife, to helpe vs in the conceiuing of that heauenly felicity in our minds. For if the magnificence of the ſpouſe be fo great vppon Earth, vvhat manner of things and howe exellent are thoſe, vvhich God hath prepared for his Saints in his ovvne prefence? But our minds are to dimme and dull to meditate of theſe things as they be in them felues, let vs therefore turne our eyes to contemplate this earthly Paradife, vvhich though it be greater, then it can be extolled vvith any eloquence of vvords, yet it is more neere and agreeable to our ſenſe, and fuch as ſhalbe feene openly in the vvorld vvithin theſe fevve yeares. The interpretation of the *Nevve heauen and earth*, may be taken out of that place, 12. 26. *VVhofe voice did then ſhake the earth, but novve he hath denounced ſaying, yet once more vvill I ſhake not the earth onely, but alſo heauen.* VVhere to ſhake heauen and earth, is by the interpretation of the Apoſtle him felfe, to *abrogate the old manner of*

*And the Sea ſhall not be extant any more.* This Sea is degenerate, and adulterate Doctrine of corrupt teachers, which ſhall haue no Place in this newe people, as whoſe Sea ſhalbe of glaſſe like to Chryſtall, moſt pure, moſt cleare, void of al brackish & foggie thickenes; ſuch as that Sea is that is deſcribed ch. 4. 6. The Iewes haue a proper Sea of their owne euẽ til this daye, which is moſt groſſe foule & darke, like to troubled waters, by reaſon of many forged & fained deuiſes of their owne touching the Meſſias, the legal worſhip, the righteouſnes of the Lawe, and many other heads of ſauing Doctrine, which ſhal be al of them ſo dried vp at this daye, that there ſhal remaine neuer a droppe of the former Sea.

*Verſ. 2. And I Iohn ſawve the holy Citty.* So much for the newe heauen & earth which Iohn ſawe: Nowe the holy Citty is brought to be ſeene alſo, which is called ſo by an exellency. The Church of the Gentiles alſo, is that holy, newe and heauenly Ieruſalem, as it is called by the Apoſtle; *But ye are come to the Hill of Sion, and to the Citty of the liuing God, to the heauenly Ieruſalem, & to millions of Angels, Hebr. 12. 22.* So like wiſe Gal. 4. 26. But this Ieruſalem of ours which is deformed & defiled with many errours & cōtentions, wil make this of the Iewes that ſhalbe moſt pure, to appeare as if it were a new one altogether.

The members of the body are often times vſed to expreſſe the ſame thing, but the ſimilitude of a Citty ſetteth a more liuely portraiture thereof before our eyes. There is greater variety of matters, and a furder Diſioining of offices and dueties, in a Citty, which yet are coupled and held together by one and the ſame lawe, and they doe respect one cheife good of the whole. This Citty therefore doth notably repreſēt vnto vs, howe the faithfull who are moſt diuerſe in the functiō, dueties, and courſe of life doe growe vp together into one holy body.

Verf. 3. *And I heard a great voice ſaying from heauen ; behold the Tabernacle of God.* The Holy Ghoſt commeth here to that part of the glory of this Citty, that is declared by the things which be heard. The Tabernacle was belonging to the Iewes properly, and to the old worſhip, So that he doth intimate here the whole diuine worſhip of this People, to whome the Tabernacle was proper before. With all he declareth that there is not any ſuch full manifeſtation of the glory of God as yet to come, as the Saints ſhall enioye after the laſt iudgement. But howſoeuer, it ſhalbe farre more plentifull, then euer hath bene before this, yet *men ſhall ſee God by a glaſſe and darkely, not face to face, they ſhall knowve in part onely, not as they haue bene knovvne;* As the Apoſtle ſpeaketh, 1. Corinth. 13. 12. The tabernacle is fit to ſhadowe out the Church that is in her pilgrimage, not that which hath attained a eſtabliſhed abiding in her owne cuntrye.

*And he ſhall dwell vvith them, and they ſhalbe his people.* Both God himſelfe ſhall take tuition of the Saints according to the forme of his couenant made with them Geneſ. 17. 1. As alſo the Saints ſhall ſubiect them ſelues willingly to God to be ruled by him. So doth Ieremy interprete theſe words, whence they are taken, *I vvill put my lavve into their mind, and I vvill vvrite it in their heart, and I vvill be their God, & they ſhalbe my people.*

Verf. 4. *And God ſhall vvipe avvay.* So much for the preſence of God; nowe as touching the remooual of Calamities, the true Church ſhal not be vexed and greiued any more, neither ſhall it be oppreſſed with the tyranny of the Beaſt, or of the Dragon, or of any other ſuch peſtilent enemy as this, but ſhe ſhal flouriſh nowe, and ſhall conquer, all her enemies. These words are borrowed from Eſay 25. 8. That we may knowe of what times the Holy Ghoſt ſpeaketh Eſay entreateth in that place of the felicity of the Chriſtian Church vppon earth; as it

*And there shalbe no more death.* The sharpenes of punishments shall cease, in which sense *Esay* saith; *He vvill destroy death for euer more, Chapt. 25. 8. And Hose; I vvill redeeme them from the povver of the Graue, I vvill deliuer them from death, I vvill be thy plague; o death. I vvill thy destruction; o graue, repentance is hid from my eyes, chapt. 13. 14.* Which place *Paul* applyeth to the last resurrection, *1. Cor. 15. 55.* as the Holy Ghost also hath declared this renewing by the same resurrectioñ, chapter 20. 12. And indeed at that time, when the bodies shall rise againe, there shalbe a full ouerthrowe of death; But in the meane time in the felicity of this newe people, there shalbe a great proofe of the weakening and destroying thereof. Not that there shal cease to be a dissolution of Soules and bodies, whereby the Saints are translated into the heauenly Kingdome, but because when the sting of death shalbe quite taken away, it shall serue no longer to be a scourge vnto the Church.

*Neither mourning nor crying, nor labour.* These words teach vs howe farre death shall be taken awaye, namely as it is a punishment, not as it is a meanes to translate men to euerlasting life. So shal the seruitours, and Sergeants attending vppon it be taken away also. For what right haue Seruants, where there is no power in their master? ô most happy Spouse, that shal neuer be molested with such disturbers of her happines as these be, a uisible Image of the happy Kingdome in heauen, shall conuerse nowe among men vppon earth.

*Because the foregoing things are gone avvaye.* The Greeke word is, *the first things*; whereby perhaps the Holy Ghost respecteth the first Estate of the Iewes, which was lamentable and miserable because of the wrath of God that was prouoked by their often rebellions; as if it were said. worde, when they translate those words, *the two great lights, Genes. 1. 16.* and Paul, when he saith, *ye shine as lights, Phil. 2. 15.* The light then of the Citty is that which geueth light vnto the cittye, which it taketh from out of the Light, but hath it not inherent of it owne, whence the<gloss>n</gloss> is it ministred vnto it? from the very glory of God; for these things depend vppon those words that went next before, as if it were said; *I saw a citty hauing the glory of God, and this glory of God, that is the light thereof, was like to a stone that is most pretious, &c.* And the 23. verse beneath helpeth vs to this interpretation, where it is made the worke of God, to inlighte<gloss>n</gloss> this Citty. But why is the light made like to a most pretious stone, and not rather to the Sunne, or to the Starres? perhaps because the light of the Sunne burneth and blindeth the eyes, being more delightfull when it is looked vppon indirectly, then when a man looketh wishly & gazeth vppon it; but the brightnes of a stone hath no hurt in it, yet much delight, and so much the more, the more stay a man maketh in viewing it; and this doth notably resemble vnto vs the pleasantnes of diuine knowledge.

For this when it is but once looked vppon as it appeareth in the beauty thereof, doth refresh the minde of a man, when it waxeth faint, and when it is oppressed with greife, but it bringeth the more refreshing, the more earnestly and intentiuely a man shall bende his witts to consider of it. The brightnes also of other things, as of the moone and the starres, is ouerwhelmed with the beames of a more abundant light. The glistring of a pretious stone striueth with the Sunne for brightnes, neither is it diminished with the beame thereof, but encreased; as there is not any greater glory, which can obscure the glory of Gods maiesty; Those things which shine amongst vs, as firebrands, Lampes,candles, doe alwayes want matter to nourish their light, els will they straight wayes goe out and turne to darkenes; The sparkling lustre of a gemme is naturall, that hath no need of supply and helpe from with out, but it shineth alwayes with his owne flame, so that it setteth before our eyes the euerlasting Brightnes and glory of the most high God in this regard also. But the kinde of the stone is expressed also. For it is like to Iasper stone that is through bright like Chrystall; The Iasper is a most noble Gemme both for antiquity, as also for varietye. thether; vnlesse perhaps it shalbe by building and enriching Temples,
by sending out preachers, into sundry Regions, and by suppressing the
