downe such stuffe, as this, what would he haue vs looke and long after
such kinde of doings as these, after this life? But I will not disquiet the
man to much, being as it seemeth sicke of a dunsicall fewer.

*Citty, that shall enioye so happy, deepe, and secure peace.*

## *The* 22. *Chapter.*

### *The* Logicall *Resoluing of it.*

*HEtherto of the two first externall arguments, wherewith the glory of this Citty is
illustrated. Nowe followe the two last arguments; the abundance of things neces-
sary, & the perpetuity. That consisteth in two things, which comprehended al the rest
of the Abundance, in most pure water that proceedeth out of the Throne, vers. 1. And
the Tree of life, vers. 2. whose Fruite is described, both howe large it is, & that partly
in the kindes of it, for there are twelue fruits, partly in the time thereof, it is brought
forth euery moneth; as also howe profitable it is, which appeareth in that euen the
leaues of it, are good for medicine to the Gentiles, vers. 2. And so much of the Abun-
dance; The perpetuity is declared by remoouing the things that may cauſe corrup-
tion, vers. 3. & by setting downe such things as may cauſe preseruation, vers. 3. 4. 5.
And thus farre hath the propheticall Narration reached both of the matters that
haue belonged to particular Churches, & of such matters also, that haue bene com-
mon to the whole Church. Nowe followeth the Epilogue, that shutteth vp the whole
Reuelation, & Epistle; which consisteth partly in a confirmation; partly in a saluta-
tion. The confirmation doth first of all make a rehearsall, & collection of matters be-
fore spoke of, that being set as it were in a rough draught, vnder one vewe, they might
haue the more force to winne credit. Nowe this rehearsal is continued vnto the 18. ver.
relating vnto vs the Author of the Reuelation, vs. 6. the felicity of those that obserue
it, vers. 7. the Ministers vs. 8. 9. the publishing thereof enioined for the free exami-
nation of things therein contained vs. 10. with an addition of an answere to a secret
obiection, vers. 11. The nature of him which doth reueale this prophecy, that is iust,
vers. 12. Eternall vers. 13. the thing reuealed vs. 14. 15. the testimony of Iesus opēly
manifested vs. 16. & lastly the desire of the Spirite & of the Bride, vers. 17. Euery
one of which is of great force seueraly to stablish the Authority of this Prophecy but
all of them iointly together, are indeed of most great force; In the second place Iohn
bringeth some newe matter in, for his owne part, both denouncing certaine destruction
against those, who shal depraue this prophecy in the least manner, vs. 18. 19. As also
witnessing his most feruent desire, to haue it accomplished speedily, vs. 20. The Salu-
tation doth at length conclude the whole Epistle with a prayer, vers. 21.*

### THE EXPOSITION.

Vers. 1. *After that he shewed me.* The exceeding great glory of this Citty is furder declared by that wholesome fruite, which not onely the Citizens, but the forraineres also doe enioye. To which purpose, both this Riuer, and this Tree, are sett downe, wherewith they get both meate and drinke vnto life. The Angell sheweth both these vnto Iohn; For he saith: *he shevved me.* But who shewed it? That Seauenth Angel, who made the Citty manifest vnto him, in the former Chapter vers. 9. 10. & therefore we are not yet come to the celestiall happines of the Saints after the last resurrection, when as we shal not vse the helpe of Angels, or of any other Teachers. As touching this water, it is not some smal brooke, but a riuer, & that not defiled and troubled, as Nilus, but flowing with most pure waters, as Kidron, & Calbirhoe, that maketh glad the Citty of God, *Psal. 46. 5.* Besides it is a Riuer of water of life, not onely because of the perpetuallnes thereof, as which doth spring continually with newe and fresh waters, of which sort is the water of a well or of a spring; which is also called liuing in the Scripture, but also because it brings life to them that drinke it, *Ioh. 4. 14.* *The Riuer is cleare as Chrystall*, farre surpassing the clearenes of other Fountaines. Lastly, it commeth from out of the *Throne of God, and the Lambe*, who are the first head-springs thereof, vnto whome also it leadeth men againe, as a companion, or rather it goeth before them like a Captaine, as the Riuer leadeth men to the Sea. In Ezechiel this selfe same Riuer floweth out of the Temple and the Altar, *Chapter 47. 1.* But there is no Temple in this newe Ierusalem, as hath bene said, *Chapter 21. 22.* And therefore the Holy Ghost putteth the Throne of God into the place thereof. It is not here expressed whether it floweth, but the Prophets teach it aboundantly, namely *tovvrards the East, from the South-side of the Altar, first into Galilee, and into the plaine, then the vvaters goe into the Sea, then the vvaters thereof are cured vvith the vvaters that are emptied into the Sea, Ezech. 47. 1. 8.* So saith Ioel: *also a Fountaine shall goe out of the house of the Lord, and shall vvater the vally of shitten, chapt. 3. 18.* Namely the plaine of Moab, where the Israelits committed whoredome, with the Moabitish women, *Nomb. 25. 1.* Zachary also saith: *It shal be in that daye, that the vvaters of life shall goe out of Ierusalem halfe of them tovvard the East Sea, & halfe of thẽ tovvard the vttermost Sea, & shalbe both in sommer*

This Riuer is the most plentifull Doctrine of Christ, which shall flowe into the East because that people being watered with the moisture thereof shall growe vp, till it flourish at lenght with true life. *For euery liuing creature vvhich mooueth, vvhether soeuer these vwaters come, shall liue, and there shalbe a multitude of fishes, and that very great; For they liue and are cured vvith the waters that come whether soeuer this riuer commeth;* Ezech. 47. 9. Vers. 2. *And in the midest of the streete thereof.* That is, the place where the whole multitude of the Cittizens keepe. For this is no fountaine sealed vp; but such as euery one that hath a part in the Citty, hath free & full power to pertake of. In this place also doth the tree of life growe, & flourish. Ezechiel mentioneth many trees. *Behold saith he, I sawe many trees here & there, on the banke of the Riuer,* Trem. trãslates it, great Trees, but the greatnes of them is not so much noted, as their nõber, as it appeares out of vers. 12. Where that which he calleth *many trees*, vers. 7. He calleth *al maner of trees, that beare fruite, fit to eate*; as if the former respected rather the variety, then the largenes of the trees. Iohn seemeth to speake collectively of one tree for many, as appeareth by those words, on either side of the Riuer, which cã not agree to one tree, vnlesse here & there to be ioined with the word Riuer, & not with the tree of life, thus, in the mids of the streete thereof, and of the Riuer that floweth on this side & beyond was the tree of life, as if the tree were placed in the mids, so as the Riuer diuided into two armes should embrace it on both sides; & so it is one tree, whereby there is a more manifest allusion to the tree of life, Gen. 3. 22. & which he mentioned before, chapt. 2. 7. To him that ouercommeth I vvill giue to eate of that tree of life, vvhich is in the midst of the Paradise of God. Iohn sawe one tree, because al the elect haue one cõmon meate of life, 1. Cor. 10. 4. Ezech. sawe many, to signifie vnto vs the plẽtiful store of meate, which this one tree ministreth This tree is Christ, who is both meate & drink to his people, that is, a most rich storehouse of al things, which be neceffary to saluation.

*And giuing fruite euery moneth.* This meate shall neuer faile, but gro-

would haue flourished alwayes laden with their fruits? This allusion
here seemeth to intimate some such matter. & perhaps Christ would
neuer haue cursed the figtree, that was void of fruite, when the time of
figgs was come vnlesse it ought to haue borne figgs at all times by the
first nature thereof; Marc. 11. 13. But I dare not set downe any thing
peremptorily touching this point, neither would I thrust my selfe wil-
lingly into this kinde of questions, but to see if I might perhaps finde
out somewhat to geue light to that hard place of Scripture.

not be applied, to the last estate of the blessed saints, where no differẽce
shalbe betwene the Gentiles, & other people, neither shal there be any
place to cure wounds, when euery one shalbe as an Angell of God.

Verf. 5. *And there shalbe no night there.* They shall not be afflicted

But howe doth he say that there shalbe no need of a Candle, when he

need any other besides the Lambe.

*For the Lord God inlighteneth them.* That is, Gods bounty shal be more
plentifully & clearely shewed,then that it shalbe ascribed to any out-

shal seeme to come to vnderstãding,not so much by hearing the word

the nature of al other gifts of God, the excellency whereof shall farre
surpasse al meanes, which they could vfe in atcheiuing them ; In the
ende of the verse, a summe of these three verses going before is pro-
pounded in plaine words ; namely that this Kingdome of the Saints
shalbe eternal,that it shalbe begun vpon earth, & shal neuer be inter-
rupted, til it be at length translated into Heauen.

brought in, that it doth not obscurely declare, that these are not the words of the Angel speaking nowe vnto Iohn, but of Iohn repeating the Argumẽts that proue this prophecye to be inspirid from God.

Verſe. 7. *Behold I come quickly.* These words are the Testimony of Iesus, touching the speedy execution of these things, taken out of Chapt 1. 1. Which must be done shortly; & againe, verse 3. The time is at hand; the Euent of things immediatly to be done, should bring credit to those that were to followe after, & therefore he mentioneth a speedy execution; as if it were said; let euery one take in each of their owne Ages, a pledge, & as it were a suretye of things to come, out of the things which he seeth to fall out presently; For these wil make it good, that the things to come are no lesse certaine; But as for vs, who haue seene the consent betwene the euent and the Prophecy for the space of a thousand & fiue hundred yeares, that is, euer since the dayes of Iohn, we can not possibly doubt, any longer touching those fewe euents, which yet remaine to be accõplished. And see I pray you, howe these things be heaped vp one vppon another without any bonds of speach, as it is the manner to doe in rehearsing matters; which thing we spake of right nowe.

Blessed is he that obserueth. Here we haue a confirmation of this Prophecy, taken frõ the felicity of those that obserue this prophecye, which nothing can helpe a man unto, but the truth which is inspired from God, as we heard before, chapt. 1. 3. Whẽce these words are repeated.

Verf. 8. *And I am Iohn.* Here we haue a confirmacion of the prophecy from the Ministers. It must needs be a most certaine prophecye, of which an Angel is the Minister, who was so ful of glory & Maiesty that the Apostle Iohn, thought himselfe bound to adore him, & withal he was so ful of holines, that he refused & forbad the diuine worship, which Iohn offered him; Iohn here relates, what had happened before Chapt. 19. 10. but he doth not fall downe againe to adore him, which was forbidden before.

Verf. 9. *And he said to me.* The words are, he saith, for he said, for he doth not record a newe matter, but that which was past. But it is to be obserued that that which he said before, *& of thy brethrẽ which haue the testimony of Iesus, ch. 19. 10.* is here brought in with other words, *& of thy brethrẽ the Prophets, & of them that obserue the vvords of this booke.* Therefore to obserue the words of this book is to haue the testimony of Iesus.

Verſ. 10. *Seale not.* Here we haue a publiſhing of this booke inioy-
ned, whereby euery one hath free power to examine, & to iudge of this
prophecye by the euent. Iohn was not to keepe this prophecye for his
owne vſe alone, but he was to offer it to publike inquirye, whatſoe-
uer danger might come thereby, as he was bidden preſently after the
beginning; *that vvhich thou ſeeſte vvrite it in a Booke, & ſend to the ſeauen
Churches, cha. 1:11. & againe, vvrit vvhat things thou haſt ſeene, & vvhich
are, & vvhich are to be*, that is; doe not conceale them from others, but
make them openly knowne to the people. Nowe if the publike ſetting
forth of theſe things in writing be that which is hereby onely meant,
howe is it that Daniel was cōmanded, *to ſhut vp his vvords, & to ſeale the
Booke*, who yet did cōmit his prophecy to writing aſwel as Iohn. This
prohibitiō therefore of not ſealing intendeth ſome further mater then
that, namely that matters to come ſhould be ſo deſcribed, that men
might be lead by the preſent, & inſtant euents as it were by the hand,
to the plaine vnderſtanding of the prophecye, which fel out otherwiſe
with Daniel, who ſhould not be plaine & euident to euery age, as who
lightly touching ſuch matters as come betweene, is chiefly taken vp in
laying forth ſuch things as were to come to paſſe laſt of al, & therfore
the determined time ſhould be expected, before which it was not able
to be explaned. And this that I ſaye of Daniel, is to be vnderſtood part-
ly touching thoſe harder viſions, partly touching the people of the Ie-
wes, whome that prophecye doth cheifly reſpect; The words that
followe do confirme this interpretation, *for the time is neere*, as if it had
bene ſaid; Seale not the prophecye, for the time that approcheth ſhall
reueale it, but Daniels was ſealed, becauſe the fulfilling of it being lōge
after to come cauſed it to lie in obſcuritye a longe time. Theſe words
the haue the ſame force, which thoſe former had, *behold I come quickly.*

Vſ. 11. *He that is vniuſt, let him be vniuſt ſtil.* In theſe words Iohn pre-
uenteth & remoueth a ſecret ſcruple, wherewith the minds of weake
Chriſtians might be ſhaken, & made more feeble. For they ſee wicked
men to perſeuere in their wickednes, & that Gods vengeance lingreth
lōge for many ages. They might therefore make this doubtful queſtiō,
howe he can be ſaid to come quickly, who tolerateth wicked men for
ſo longe a time. Here then he meeteth with this obiection; & giueth a
Caueat, that none of the faithful ſhould be troubled at this, but vnder-
ſtand rather, that wicked men ſhal perſiſt in their vngodly practiſes, &

words then haue an excellent coherence with those that went before.
& they are not by any meanes to be thrust into another place; & yet if

->Glory, & thankes be geuen to God euermore, Amen.<-

> I Geue thee thankes, (o almighty, & euerlasting God) that though I be a blind, vnskilfull & vvretched man, that hath no iudgement, no vvit at all, yet thou hast of thy meere mercy for Christs sake, conducted me thorough this vnpassable vvildernes, hast made me able to vievve many close corners narrovvly on euery side, & hast made me trauaile safely thorough the denes of the Dragon, & vvild Beasts. Euen so (o Father, so is thy good vvil. Thou chusest the vnnoble & obscure ones of the vvorld, & hast established stre~gth out of the mouth of Babes & sucklings, that so no flesh might boast. Hovve incomprehe~sible is thy vvisdome, hovve admirable is thy truth? hovve iust & holy be al thy vvayes? vvho vvould not feare thee? I vvould vvillingly tel forth thy praises, but my tongue vva~teth vvords, my vvords vvant vndersta~ding. Which vvay soeuer my minde can turne it selfe, it is svvallovved vp of thy infinitenes; It is ascended into heaue~, thou art higher then it; if it thinke vpon thy vvorkes, thou art greater the~ they; If it meditate on thy holines, thou art purer the~ the Sunne it selfe. O huge depth, & vnmeasurable gulfe vvithout bottome, hovve doest thou compasse vs on euery side, & yet thou art no vvhere comprehe~ded thy selfe? What mortall eye is there that can not be ouervvhelmed vvith the infinite brightnes thereof. Therfore my dimme sight, doth turne it selfe from this light that can not be approached to, that it may behold thee, through the Cloud of the Creatures, aboue all, it doth much delight, to co~template thy most amiable countenance in thy blessed Sonne. Yet as thou art most visible in this glasse, so thou are most admirable, as farre exceeding al our vndersta~ding, as thou doest submit thy selfe lovvest & neerest vnto our sense. Thou art great ô Lord, aboue al that can be either spoken or thought; make vs to reuere~ce thy infinitenes, vvhich the vvorld can not containe, to feare thy presence, vvhich our eyes can not behold, to adore thy Maiesty, in respect vvhereof the vniuersal vvorld, vvith al the creatures here belovve, are lesse the~ nothing, to magnifie thy bountifulnes, vvhich thou shevvest ple~tifully vpon vs that are most vnvvorthy men. Accomplish at length thy great mystery, & let the vvorld acknovvledge, that thy long tariance hath proceeded from thy mercy onely, & not from any forgetfulnes, or carelessenes of thy promise. Destroy that Beast of Rome, & dragon of Consta~tinople; Build vp thy nevve Ierusalem, in vvhich Christ shall raigne, vvherein also the Saints shal haue dominion together vvith him, that so they may inioye a blessed kingdome for a time vpo~ earth & a most happy & eternal one vvith thee in the heaue~s. Heare vs graciously ô Father from vvhome no thought of our heart can be hidden; dravve neere vvith thy presence vvho art absent no vvhere, and doe thou graunt our holy desires, vvhich thou hast made vvay for vvith thy decree, and set a flaming vvith this reuealed Reuelation; The~ shal vve make ready our harpes, & sing praises vnto thee, magnifying thee one God in three Persons, Father, Sonne & Holy Ghost, to vvhome be al honour, laude & glory throughout al ages, and for euer more, Amen.
